headline: Four of six citizen service centers launched by interim government are locked, two rarely open
summary: Launched to reduce hassle and corruption, these centers were meant to provide 450 government services. However, a lack of promised equipment, internet, and official contracts has led to their widespread closure.
details: Six citizen service centers, initiated by Faiz Ahmed Tayyeb, special assistant to the former chief advisor of the interim government, are largely defunct. Four of these pilot centers, including one in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, are now locked, with no service providers or recipients present.

These centers were designed to offer around 450 government services, such as passport applications, national ID cards, birth registrations, general diaries (GDs), and land services. Entrepreneurs were meant to operate each center and earn a fixed fee per service.

However, entrepreneurs report that the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Division failed to provide essential equipment like computers, printers, biometric devices, and crucial internet connectivity. Without these tools and effective links to government portals, services could not be delivered.

Md. Mustakim, an entrepreneur at the Mohammadpur center, left his computer service shop hoping for regular income from the initiative but received no promised equipment. Similarly, Rajit Khan, from the Nilkhet center, closed his operation due to lack of income, while Ashikur Rahman in Uttara also reported receiving no necessary tools.

The 'Citizen Service Centers' were launched on May 26, 2025, under the slogan 'All Citizen Services in One Address,' with the pilot project inaugurated by then-Chief Advisor Professor Muhammad Yunus. He stated the initiative would play a groundbreaking role in reducing broker dominance and ensuring hassle-free services.

Despite the ambitious launch, an ICT Division official, speaking anonymously, suggested the initiative was 'superficial' and lacked a dedicated budget or proper promotion from the interim government. Entrepreneurs also complained about the absence of formal contracts, preventing them from independently securing internet connections.

While the current government has not officially announced the closure of the citizen service initiative, the centers remain largely inactive. The two centers that are occasionally open see very few visitors and are at risk of permanent closure.
caption:
Six citizen service centers were launched to streamline government services and combat corruption. Today, four are locked, and the remaining two are rarely open.

Six citizen service centers, initiated by Faiz Ahmed Tayyeb, special assistant to the former chief advisor of the interim government, are largely defunct. Four of these pilot centers, including one in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, are now locked, with no service providers or recipients present.

These centers were designed to offer around 450 government services, such as passport applications, national ID cards, birth registrations, general diaries (GDs), and land services. Entrepreneurs were meant to operate each center and earn a fixed fee per service.

However, entrepreneurs report that the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Division failed to provide essential equipment like computers, printers, biometric devices, and crucial internet connectivity. Without these tools and effective links to government portals, services could not be delivered.

Md. Mustakim, an entrepreneur at the Mohammadpur center, left his computer service shop hoping for regular income from the initiative but received no promised equipment. Similarly, Rajit Khan, from the Nilkhet center, closed his operation due to lack of income, while Ashikur Rahman in Uttara also reported receiving no necessary tools.

The 'Citizen Service Centers' were launched on May 26, 2025, under the slogan 'All Citizen Services in One Address,' with the pilot project inaugurated by then-Chief Advisor Professor Muhammad Yunus. headline: Sagar-Runi murder: New clue, three more suspects identified
summary: After years, a significant breakthrough has emerged in the high-profile Sagar-Runi murder case, with new evidence leading to the identification of three additional suspects.
details: The long-pending murder case of journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi has seen a significant breakthrough. Authorities have reportedly identified three new suspects based on fresh clues in the ongoing investigation.
The couple was brutally murdered in their Dhaka apartment in February 2012, a case that has remained unsolved for over a decade, drawing widespread national attention and calls for justice.
This latest development offers a renewed hope for progress in a case that has seen numerous twists and turns, with various agencies investigating over the years.
caption:
A decade-old murder mystery involving journalist couple Sagar-Runi sees a major breakthrough with three new suspects identified.

The long-pending murder case of journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi has seen a significant breakthrough. Authorities have reportedly identified three new suspects based on fresh clues in the ongoing investigation.

The couple was brutally murdered in their Dhaka apartment in February 2012, a case that has remained unsolved for over a decade, drawing widespread national attention and calls for justice.

This latest development offers a renewed hope for progress in a case that has seen numerous twists and turns, with various agencies investigating over the years.
